question: Can the 2020 Danish-seine catch-composition article support a historical fish-name inventory for Lingayen Gulf, and what spatial, sampling, taxonomic, and reuse limits apply?

method.summary: Retrieved the complete seven-page publisher PDF. Read the abstract, methods, Tables 1 and 2, figure captions, discussion, conclusion, and references. Rendered the printed Table 1 and Table 2 pages to inspect the source strings and sector marks visually. No permanent local copy, raw vessel logbook, fish image, or supplementary dataset was retained.
method.studyFrame: The paper monitored landings of two 45-hp commercial fishing vessels using modified Danish seine: one vessel operated in each of Sector I and Sector III. Catch landings were monitored every 15 days from December 2015 to January 2016, with landed weights taken from vessel logbooks. Fish specimens were collected from the master fisherman at Magsaysay Market, Dagupan City, and identified from morphology using cited books and FishBase; unidentified specimens were reportedly taken to the PSU-Binmaley wet laboratory.
method.spatialLimit: The article defines Sector I broadly as the western coast between Cape Bolinao and Sual and Sector III as the eastern coast. Magsaysay Market is the landing and specimen-collection location, not an individual fish capture coordinate. The map plots vessel-area dots but reports no machine-readable coordinates, haul-to-species crosswalk, CRS/datum, or sector boundary geometry. Do not georeference the dots or assign a species to a municipality, reef, river mouth, municipal-water polygon, or precise capture site.
method.rightsFinding: The first page prints © 2020 IJFAS. The reviewed article and publisher metadata did not identify an item-specific Creative Commons or other reuse license. Public PDF availability is not treated as permission to redistribute the article's table, figures, or fish images. Keep the source summary and label strings research-only pending a separate rights decision.

study.titleAsPrinted: Catch composition and relative biomass of fishes caught by danish seine in Lingayen gulf
study.citation: De Guzman, M. F., Macalalay, R. L. S., Surat, R. A. F., Villaruz, J. B., & Rosario, G. R. (2020). Catch composition and relative biomass of fishes caught by Danish seine in Lingayen Gulf. International Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Studies, 8(6), 24–30. https://doi.org/10.22271/fish.2020.v8.i6a.2355
study.samplingFrequencyAsReported: Every 15 days over a two-month period; the paper does not provide exact haul/sample dates or the number of completed landing events.
study.samplingSite: Magsaysay Market, Dagupan City, Pangasinan; vessel landings and specimen source, not a fish capture coordinate.
study.gearAsReported: Modified Danish seine operated by two 45-hp commercial vessels, one assigned to each of Sector I and Sector III.
study.identificationMethodAsReported: Morphological features checked against Conlu (1986), Rau and Rau (1980), and FishBase; specimens not identified in the first pass were reportedly preserved in ethanol and taken to the Pangasinan State University-Binmaley wet laboratory.

publishedCatchSummary.relativeBiomassIsBasedOn: Landed catch weight from the sampled fishing vessels; not a direct estimate of ecosystem standing biomass or whole-community abundance.

internalConflicts: The abstract and Results section say 38 species in 22 families; Table 1 has 38 taxon rows but only 21 distinct printed family labels, and the Discussion also says 21 families. Preserve the counts separately rather than reconciling by assumption.
The conclusion reports 25 species/15 families in Sector I and 29 species/20 families in Sector III, consistent with the Table 1 sector marks; this does not remove the total-family conflict.

The text says Atule mate was the lowest-caught species at about 1% of the combined catch, but Table 2 gives it 116.4 kg while multiple other listed taxa have substantially smaller combined catch weights. Do not use this lowest-species statement as a table-derived result.
The paper discusses a 2013 Danish-seine prohibition and environmental/legal implications. This historical research article is not a current fisheries-rule or legal-status source.

rights.disposition: No article-specific reuse license was found in the reviewed PDF or publisher metadata. Keep source-derived details internal to the research workflow; publication approval remains false.

interpretation: The table provides 38 historical source name strings and sector-level landed-catch marks for two modified-Danish-seine vessels during a short 2015–2016 window. These are source-reported fishery catch candidates, not a complete Lingayen Gulf ecosystem checklist.

The single landing market, broad sector labels, and schematic map do not establish fish-by-site capture localities or reusable coordinates. Do not assign these rows to Dagupan rivers, reefs, municipalities, exact bays, or municipal-water boundaries.

Vessel gear selectivity, the two-vessel sample, short collection window, and absence of vouchers or fish-event records limit completeness and taxonomic validation. Table name strings remain verbatim pending separate name review.
Landed catch weights and the paper's relative-biomass terminology do not represent standing biomass, natural abundance, present-day presence, catchability, bait suitability, legality, or safety.

The source is distinct in time and design from Gaerlan et al. (2018)'s 2009–2013 small-pelagic landing summaries. Do not sum their species totals or treat the papers as independent environmental censuses.

No normalized species assertions, occurrence rows, waterbody sub-assignments, geometry, diet, photos, catch advice, legal/safety claims, or public-app rows were added. Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.

decision.reason: The article is a short, historical, gear-selective landing study with only broad sector context, no haul coordinates/vouchers, internal family-count and relative-biomass conflicts, and no item-specific reuse license. Preserve its table names as research-only source strings pending taxonomy, locality, and rights review.

nextAction: Keep the 38 Table 1 source labels and sector marks only as research leads. Cross-check names with authoritative fish taxonomic references without treating accepted-name status as specimen verification; seek the source vessel logbooks/GPS and voucher crosswalk only if independently available; review article-specific reuse before any publication. Continue Region I freshwater, estuary, coastal, and marine source coverage independently.
